 Order

The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.160 of 2018 on the files of the District and Sessions Court,
Pathanamthitta, which arose out of Crime No.2586 of 2015 of the Pathanamthitta Police Station.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections 366, 344 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860.

The prosecution case is that the petitioner, a married man having family, induced CW2 to believe that he would marry her after the dissolution of his existing marriage with another lady, and indulged in sexual relationship with CW2 on 16.09.2015 at the bedroom of a house at Venmony,
where the victim had been taken by the petitioner and lodged.
2. The case has been registered by the Pathanamthitta Police on the basis of the First Information Statement given by the brother of the victim.
After the completion of the investigation, the 2025:KER:50870 Inspector of Police, Pathanamthitta, laid the Final Report alleging the commission of the aforesaid offences by the petitioner.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he is totally innocent, and that he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that the victim as well as the defacto complainant who lodged the First Information Statement in this case, are having no subsisting grievance against the petitioner, and that the matter has been amicably settled with them, and that CW Nos.1 and 2 have filed affidavits stating their willingness to quash the proceedings against him.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the defacto complainant and the victim (respondents 2 and 3) and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. As already stated above, the prosecution case is that the petitioner, a married man, induced the victim to believe that he would marry her after dissolving his subsisting marriage with another lady,
and indulged in sexual relationship with her.
Thus, it is 2025:KER:50870 apparent that there is absolutely no misconception of facts which would have compelled the victim to extend consent for the sexual intercourse with the petitioner.
The victim being an educated girl, cannot be expected to have believed the offer of a married man, that after accomplishing a divorce, he would marry her.
Obviously, the relationship between the petitioner and the victim was consensual.
That apart, it is seen from the affidavit filed by the victim that she had categorically stated that she went along with the petitioner with her free will and consent.
In the aforesaid affidavit, she had sworn that she is having no objection in terminating the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner.
An affidavit upon the same terms has been filed by the brother of the victim at whose instance, the case has been registered.

The only conclusion, which could be drawn from the above facts and circumstances of the case is that the offence of rape is not attracted, since the relationship between the petitioner and the victim was consensual.

In that view of the matter, the prayer of the petitioner to quash the Achu T. Thomas vs State Of Kerala on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91908290/
2 proceedings against him, has to be allowed.
